title: Minimize Length of Array Using Operations
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums with positive integers, minimize its length by repeatedly selecting two distinct indices i and j where nums[i] > 0 and nums[j] > 0, inserting nums[i] % nums[j] at the end, and deleting nums[i] and nums[j].
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums with positive integers, minimize its length by repeatedly selecting two distinct indices i and j where nums[i] > 0 and nums[j] > 0, inserting nums[i] % nums[j] at the end, and deleting nums[i] and nums[j]. Return the minimum possible length of nums after any number of operations.
constraints: Replace any chosen pair by one value equal to the first modulo the second.
Return the smallest length reachable after repeated operations.
reference_solution:
def minimum_modulo_array_length(nums):
    smallest=min(nums)
    if any(value%smallest for value in nums):return 1
    return (nums.count(smallest)+1)//2
known_wrong_solutions:

def minimum_modulo_array_length(nums):
    smallest=min(nums)
    if any(value%smallest for value in nums):return 1
    return (nums.count(smallest)+2)//2
hints: The current minimum controls whether a still smaller positive remainder can be created.
If any value is not divisible by the minimum, repeated modulo reductions can reach one remaining value.
Otherwise only minimum copies matter; return ceil(count/2).
Pairs of minimum values turn into zero and eliminate two copies, while an odd leftover requires one final value.
editorial: Pairs of minimum values turn into zero and eliminate two copies, while an odd leftover requires one final value.

tests.explanation: A non-multiple of the minimum permits producing a smaller remainder and ultimately one value.
All values are multiples of two and only one minimum occurs, so one value can remain.
